citations.label: Model Context Protocol blog, the stateless protocol core
citations.excerpt: The highlight of this release is a stateless protocol core - MCP is transforming from a bidirectional stateful protocol into a request/response stateless protocol.

citations.label: Model Context Protocol blog, header based routing
citations.excerpt: Method and tool names travel in the `Mcp-Method` and `Mcp-Name` HTTP headers, so gateways can route and authorize on headers directly.

citations.label: Model Context Protocol blog, deprecation window
citations.excerpt: They still work, and they'll keep working for at least twelve months.

citations.label: The Register, Craig McLuckie of Stacklok on why MCP was stateful
citations.excerpt: The stateful nature of MCP was really a by-product of its origin as a way to support developers using coding tools (that tend to run locally) to access things.
